findings.title: Questions await the informed guide's report
findings.claim: The patience named in 18:67 can be read as a disciplined interval in which the learner's question remains live while report, recollection, and final meaning are first supplied by the informed guide.
findings.mechanism: The focus noun for self-restraint is contacted by the later question, report, and mention forms, by the explicit lack of encompassing and inner knowledge, and by the later account that returns events to their outcomes. The contact makes patience a timing relation for inquiry rather than a rejection of inquiry.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the guide's silence is procedural: a question is not invalid, but its explanatory force changes when it waits for the person who possesses the causal frame to speak.
findings.containment: The ordinary claim remains that Moses is told he will not be able to remain patient with the guide. This finding does not make all questions impermissible, nor does it claim that speech timing exhausts the word's meaning.

epistemic.reason: The channel supports and its local context refs are supplied as trusted macro evidence with explicit question, report, knowledge, and outcome contacts.

findings.title: Learning companionship has a patience contract
findings.claim: Within the learning companionship, the focus warning names the capacity to remain with a guide under a declared limit on questioning; when that limit is breached, companionship ends while explanation can still follow.
findings.mechanism: The focus self-restraint is activated by the learner's request to follow for teaching, the later question and prohibition, and the final separation followed by interpretation. Companionship, asking, separation, and outcome-return therefore contact the same local contract without becoming one lexical gloss.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the threatened loss is relational as well as intellectual: the learner may still receive an explanation, but no longer from inside the shared journey that made the instruction possible.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains a warning that Moses will not patiently endure the guide's company. This finding does not claim that every teacher-student relation has this rule or that separation proves a general theory of companionship.

epistemic.reason: The supplied trusted channel support directly names the following, question, companionship limit, separation, and later interpretation sequence.
